data.title: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Economist Urges Government to Stop Changing Mandate
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Reserve Bank of New Zealand Chief Economist Paul Conway urged future finance ministers to stop changing the central bank’s mandate, warning that repeated changes affect how monetary policy is conducted.

data.title: China Solar Cell Exports Extend Gains for Second Month Ahead of US Tariffs
data.description: China’s solar cell exports rose for a second consecutive month in October as overseas buyers stocked up before US tariffs on polysilicon take effect in early December, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Former Aave DAO Core Member Says Sky and sUSDS Have No Issues, Plans No Withdrawals
data.description:
Marc Zeller, a former core member of Aave DAO and founder of Acier, said the Sky ecosystem and sUSDS have no issues and that Acier has no plans to withdraw funds.

According to Odaily, Zeller said stUSDS is a private credit line for Rune to fund his own projects and is separate from the main savings yield pool. He said the only parties facing risk are those who believe $SKY itself has value.

Zeller described Justin Sun’s DeFi team as among the industry’s best and said it is conservative and risk-averse. Sun has withdrawn funds from Aave more than 10 times in recent years, Zeller said. After Stani took over Aave and the Kelp incident, Sun chose to keep sUSDS temporarily as his main fund deployment on Ethereum mainnet. Zeller said he expects Sun to redeposit the funds once conditions stabilize.

Zeller said most of Acier’s treasury funds were held in the SKY ecosystem to earn yield before being deployed. He said the team considers it one of the lowest-risk decentralized yield sources currently available.

data.title: HSBC Raises Tesla Rating to Hold With $359 Price Target
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, HSBC upgraded Tesla (TSLA.O) to Hold and set a price target of $359.

data.title: Gold Futures Plunge Triggers Brief Trading Halt at Osaka Exchange
data.description: According to Jin10, Japan's Fuji Television Network reported that a sharp drop in gold futures prices prompted the Osaka Exchange to briefly halt trading on the morning of November 20. The circuit breaker was triggered at 10:58 a.m. local time (09:58 UTC+8) after gold futures hit the lower price limit, and trading resumed at 11:08 a.m. (10:08 UTC+8). It was the first time since March this year, after an eight-month interval, that gold futures on the Osaka Exchange triggered a circuit breaker.

data.title: Indonesian Government Agency Asks Google Why It Removed More Than 19,000 Pro-Government YouTube Channels
data.description: According to Jin10, an Indonesian government agency has asked Google to explain why it removed more than 19,000 YouTube channels supporting the Indonesian government.

data.title: Senate Passes BAAJA Permitting Bill Backed by AI and Energy Sectors
data.description: According to CNBC, the Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, known as BAAJA, by a 62-33 vote on Thursday. The bill would ease environmental permitting rules and overhaul electrical transmission regulations, and is projected to lower energy costs for consumers. It now heads to the House, where Republican leaders are expected to try to pass it before it can go to President Donald Trump.

data.title: Nextdc Pledges to Keep Data Center Sites Away From Homes
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Australian data center company Nextdc said it will no longer develop sites near residential areas after community opposition and power constraints delayed a major expansion project.

data.title: Wang Chun Backs Sky Protocol Founder, Says He Is Buying the Dip, Compares SKY to Strategy Stock and stUSDC to STRC Preferred Shares
data.description: F2Pool co-founder Wang Chun voiced support for Sky Protocol founder Rune amid a recent lending controversy involving the protocol and its founder. According to Odaily, Wang commented on a post responding to Rune, saying, “He is buying the dip,” and comparing SKY to MSTR stock and stUSDS to STRC preferred shares.

data.title: Tempo Launches Facilitator for Cross-Chain X402 Payments Settled on Tempo
data.description: Tempo engineer Brendan Ryan said the team has released Tempo Facilitator. According to Foresight News, the service lets applications accept X402 payments from other chains, with Base currently supported, and settle them on Tempo. It is designed to simplify fund management and keep balances private. Merchants can integrate the service with a short code and obtain an API key, while buyers can pay through any X402-compatible client.

data.title: Espresso and AWS Test More Than 1 Million Transactions Finalized Per Second
data.description:
Blockchain infrastructure provider Espresso and Amazon Web Services (AWS) reported results from a performance test involving 87 independent chains sending ERC-20 token transfers. According to Foresight News, the test recorded more than 1 million transactions finalized per second, with an average finality time of under 0.5 seconds; performance remained stable as the workload increased to its peak.

Espresso had estimated a theoretical capacity of 1 million transactions per second last month based on data throughput of 181 MB/s. The benchmark was run on AWS EC2 instances and simulated latency across a global network.

data.title: U.S. Senate Passes Landmark Bill to Reform Energy Project Permitting
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, the U.S. Senate passed a landmark bill by a vote of 62-33 on Thursday to reform federal permitting for pipelines, transmission lines and other large energy infrastructure projects, sending the measure to the House. The 500-page bill, reached after weeks of debate as a compromise negotiated by both parties and the White House, has support from the oil and gas industry and clean energy groups but faces opposition from many major environmental organizations.

The bill would set deadlines for government reviews under the National Environmental Policy Act and other laws, require data centers to pay billions of dollars toward grid construction, and limit federal agencies’ power to revoke permits for projects already operating or under construction. Environmental groups say the proposal would expand the Trump administration’s authority to speed approvals for data centers and oil and gas drilling. Native American tribes say it would undermine their sovereignty.

House Speaker Mike Johnson supports the proposal and predicted it could win enough votes, but lawmakers from both parties, including Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, have called for changes. Some Republicans, including House Freedom Caucus policy chairman Chip Roy, raised concerns about provisions on electricity transmission; some progressive Democrats opposed the Senate version, saying it would weaken environmental laws. House Natural Resources Committee Chairman Bruce Westerman said Thursday he doubted there would be time to revise the bill before Congress ends its term late next month. He said before the vote that if the Senate passed it, he believed the House would also have to pass it. Earlier efforts to reform federal permitting, including bills introduced by former Democratic Senator Joe Manchin in 2022 and 2024, failed to pass the Senate.

data.title: U.S. Spot SOL ETFs Record $1.40M Net Outflow, Grayscale GSOL Leads With $1.11M
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing RootData, U.S. spot SOL ETFs recorded a combined net outflow of $1.40 million on November 19 (U.S. Eastern Time). Grayscale’s GSOL led with $1.11 million in outflows; its cumulative net inflows stood at $118 million as of that trading day. Invesco Galaxy’s QSOL saw $293,400 in net outflows, with cumulative net inflows of $2.62 million. Spot SOL ETFs’ total historical net inflows reached $1.42 billion.

data.title: Honda Unveils Asia Hybrid SUV as It Shifts From Failed EV Bet
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Honda Motor Co. unveiled a new flagship gas-electric hybrid SUV for Asia, the first in a range of hybrid models it plans to roll out this decade as it shifts away from fully electric cars.

data.title: Solidity Releases Version 0.8.39 to Fix Silent Storage-Corruption Vulnerability
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Solidity has released version 0.8.39 to fix a medium-severity vulnerability that could silently corrupt storage without triggering an error. The bug affected multiple 0.8 versions and occurred when a recursive struct in storage was copied into a storage struct containing it. The fix adds a runtime overlap check, which increases gas consumption. The team said its scan of verified contracts found no affected deployed contracts.

data.title: AI | Copper Falls to Lowest Since March as Selloff Rattles Metals Markets
data.description: According to Bloomberg, copper fell to its lowest level since March after a week of market turmoil fueled by deepening concerns about global demand.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Anthropic’s Australia Data Center Project Faces Overwhelming Local Opposition
data.description: According to Jin10, project filings show that a planned data center in a remote area of Australia, with Anthropic (ANT.O) as its primary tenant, has faced overwhelming opposition from local residents. The proposed Western Downs Digital Park is about 250 kilometers west of Brisbane. Of nearly 600 public submissions, only two supported the project and one was neutral; the other 595 opposed it or called for delays until the developer addressed specific environmental concerns. The site is in farmland, far from suburban residential areas, and its planned computing load of 1.44 gigawatts would make it one of Australia’s largest data centers. About one-third of the submissions came from people living within 200 kilometers of the site. Opponents raised concerns about water use, electricity demand and prices, noise, road damage from construction vehicles, and pressure on housing supply.

data.title: Hong Kong Stocks Slide 20% From 2026 Peak as AI Selloff Widens
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Hong Kong stocks were heading for a bear market after falling 20% from their 2026 high, pressured by concerns about China’s economic health, the unraveling AI trade and US restrictions on chip exports.

data.title: Michael Burry Says He Warned on AI Stocks NVIDIA and CoreWeave
data.description:
Michael Burry said he had warned investors about NVIDIA, CoreWeave and Nebius, but had not told anyone to short them; all three stocks fell Thursday. Nebius dropped 9.4%, CoreWeave 6.1% and Nvidia 3.3%, according to BeInCrypto. Burry, a former Scion Asset Management fund manager, wrote on X Thursday that he had provided information investors could use to sell. TipRanks reported he holds Nvidia put options with a $140 strike expiring in February 2027. In a Nov. 12 Substack post, he said he doubled his Nasdaq-100 puts and rebuilt part of his position in the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH), which counts Nvidia among its top holdings. His Nasdaq-100 puts run into early 2027.

CoreWeave and Nebius sell AI developers access to Nvidia-powered servers. Burry argued that the two neoclouds, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and ASML relied on Nvidia’s market power. Nvidia shares have fallen 19% since Nov. 8, when co-founder Jensen Huang admitted extramarital affairs to staff; he resigned as CEO four days later. The company’s first post-Huang earnings report showed revenue up 103% to $115.8 billion. Interim CEO Colette Kress rejected concerns about neoclouds, saying the largest cloud operators were not pulling back. Nvidia closed at $145.98 Thursday, 39% below its October high. Burry became known for betting against the 2008 housing bubble.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Mistral Plans Singapore Regional Hub, Aims to Double Its Asia Workforce
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, French AI startup Mistral has established its Asia-Pacific headquarters in Singapore to meet growing regional demand for sovereign AI capabilities. The company plans to more than double its Asia-Pacific workforce to 200 by 2027, hiring in science, engineering, AI applications and robotics.

Mistral said the investment will support its goal of accelerating the development, training and real-world deployment of sovereign AI models. Co-founder and CEO Arthur Mensch said the company aims to make Singapore a strategic hub that enables governments and businesses across Asia-Pacific to control their infrastructure and intellectual assets and turn them into lasting economic value and industrial competitiveness.

In September, Mistral completed a funding round led by South Korea’s Samsung Electronics, valuing the company at more than $24 billion. The funding will support model development and customer-base expansion.
